meta.source: WHO Benchmarks for Strengthening Health Emergency Capacities, second edition (2023), online edition at ihrbenchmark.who.int
meta.scope: The 62 benchmarks that strengthen both IHR and health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) capacities. The 18 HEPR-only benchmarks (H1 to H5) are not included yet.
meta.note: Benchmark titles are WHO's wording; some long titles are abbreviated with an ellipsis. The link to JEE v3 indicators is a topic crosswalk made for this tool, not an official WHO mapping.

areas.name: IHR coordination, National IHR Focal Point functions and advocacy
Linking public health and security authorities
Points of entry and border health

benchmarks.title: Legal instruments are in place across relevant sectors to support and enable IHR implementation and compliance
Gender equity and equality principles are applied throughout IHR capacities
Financing is available and disbursed for the implementation of IHR capacities
Financing available for timely response to health emergencies
The IHR NFP is fully functional
Multisectoral IHR coordination mechanism effectively supports the implementation of prevention, detection and response activities
Strategic planning for IHR, preparedness or health security are in place and supported by functional advocacy mechanisms for IHR implementation
Effective multisectoral coordination for AMR
A surveillance system of AMR is in place
Effective mechanisms are in place to prevent multidrug resistant organisms (MDRO)
Optimize use of antimicrobial medicines in human health
Optimize use of antimicrobial medicines in animal health and agriculture
A multisectoral surveillance system is in place for priority zoonotic diseases/pathogens
A functional mechanism to respond to priority zoonotic diseases is in place
Safe practices in animal breeding and animal product systems limit the risk of zoonotic diseases
Surveillance systems are in place for the detection and monitoring of foodborne diseases and food contamination
A functional mechanism is in place for the response and management of food safety emergencies
Optimum vaccine coverage (measles) as part of a national programme
Provision of national vaccine access and delivery
An effective mechanism for mass vaccination for epidemics of vaccine preventable diseases (VPD) is in place
Whole-of-government biosafety and biosecurity system is in place for relevant sectors including human, animal (domestic animals and wildlife) and agricultural facilities
Biosafety and biosecurity training and practices in relevant sectors including human, animal (domestic animals and wildlife) and agriculture
Specimen referral and transport system is in place for relevant sectors
Laboratory quality system is in place
Laboratory testing for detection of priority diseases is in place
An effective national diagnostic network is in place
Early warning surveillance systems are well established and functional
Well-functioning event verification and investigation system is in place
Surveillance data and information are systematically analysed and shared to inform decision making for action
An up-to-date multisectoral workforce strategy is in place
Human resources are available to effectively implement IHR
Fit-for-purpose competency-based education programmes are available for multisectoral workforce
Multisectoral workforce surge strategy for health emergencies is well established and functional
Effective risk profiling, readiness assessment and rapid risk assessment processes are in place and strongly linked to health emergency and disaster management plans and structures
Public health emergency operations centre (PHEOC) capacities, procedures and plans are in place
A functional multisectoral, all hazard health emergency response management system is in place
A system is in place for timely and effectively providing surge health personnel and teams during a health emergency
A system is in place for emergency logistic and supply chain management during a health emergency
Research, development and innovation (RD&I) capacity for emergency management is in place
All hazard health emergency and disaster risk management (EDRM) are mainstreamed across IHR capacities
Safe and resilient hospitals and health facilities are in place to rapidly respond to emergencies
Emergency resources, needs and gaps are identified and mapped, and information shared with decision-makers and partners based on country risk profiles to inform resource strategies and activities
Multisectoral planning for health emergency preparedness and response is in place
Public health and security authorities (law enforcement, border control, customs) are linked during a suspect or confirmed biological, chemical or radiological event
Case management procedures are implemented for relevant IHR hazards
Mechanism for continuity of essential health services (EHS) during a health emergency is well established
Mechanism is in place to ensure effective utilization of health services before, during and after health emergencies at all levels of health service delivery
National and health facility level IPC programmes are in place
A functioning healthcare-associated infection (HCAI) surveillance system is in place for public health decision making
Provide a safe environment in all health care facilities
Risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) systems with mechanisms for functions and resources are in place and integrated within broader emergency programmes
Mechanisms to deliver quality, timely, impactful risk communication are operational
Community engagement is integrated and prioritized within management of health emergencies and unusual events
Inclusive community-centred governance and management of health emergencies is in place
Capacity building mechanisms for multisectoral community health workforce and community engagement in the management of health emergencies and resilience building are well established
An infodemic management system for health emergencies and unusual events is in place
Routine core capacities at PoEs are in place
Effective public health response at PoEs are in place
An effective multisectoral mechanism for risk-based approach to international travel related measures is in place
Mechanisms are in place for surveillance, alert and response to chemical events or emergencies, supported by an enabling environment
Mechanisms are in place for detecting and responding to radiological and nuclear emergencies, supported by an enabling environment
Leadership and governance dedicated to PHSM is in place in relevant sectors, at all levels and between levels
